title: Choose the look for Hive Monitor
question: Same broken moment in each sketch: the boiler receiver dropped at 07:12. The roll picked road signs. Keep it, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Road signs
options.lineage: Kinneir and Calvert's British road sign system, 1965
options.thesis: The heating system drawn as a road diagram: each device a sign pictogram, each connection a road that visibly closes when it fails.
options.viewport: A sign-style verdict panel in plain words ('Hot water: working'), then the chain as a map-type junction sign: thick strokes linking device pictograms, a red closure where it breaks, and a 'Try this' plate under the fault.
options.risk: Without the real Transport face, a lookalike can read as a pastiche of a council sign.

raised.raise: State lives in the stroke, not only in colour: solid is working, cut is down, dotted is unknown.
The break is the page's only diagonal: a failed link is one clean cut across its road.
Every device pictogram is drawn on one grid at one scale, so they read as a single sign family.
Nothing disappears when it breaks: the closure is stamped over the link and the drawing stays.

options.label: Tube map
options.lineage: Harry Beck's Underground diagram and the line status board
options.thesis: Devices are stations, connections are track, and a fault is a suspended section with the reason posted.
options.viewport: A status strip ('Good service' or 'Part suspended'), then one line from Pi to boiler with the thermostat on a branch; a dead section turns to a dashed gap with the closure named beside it.
options.risk: The most familiar move for this brief, and close to TfL's own brand; it has to stay a diagram, not a TfL costume.

options.label: Departure board
options.thesis: Each link is a row on the board: on time, delayed or cancelled, flipping when it changes.
options.viewport: A black board with seven rows, one per link, each with a plain status word; the broken row drops to dim red.
options.case: Everyone in the house reads a departure board instantly, but rows lose how the devices connect, which is the thing you asked to see.
options.risk: Reads as a list again, the shape you're moving away from.

options.label: Friendly app cards
options.thesis: Soft cards, plain-language labels, one bright colour only where you can press.
options.viewport: One card per device with an illustration and a sentence, stacked in a single column.
options.case: Comfortable for the whole household, but cards don't show the chain or where it breaks.
options.risk: Pleasant and forgettable; closest to Hive's own app.

options.label: Botanical folio
options.thesis: One plant through its seasons at fixed scale.
options.viewport: Devices as fixed-scale plates along one stem.
options.case: A life cycle doesn't map onto a chain of devices.
options.kept: Fixed scale on one ground: every pictogram drawn on the same grid.

options.label: Airline ticket wallet
options.thesis: Each link a coupon; a dead one is stamped VOID.
options.viewport: A coupon stack, one leg per link.
options.case: Nobody at home thinks of their boiler as a journey.
options.kept: Nothing disappears, it cancels: the closure is stamped over the link.

options.label: Dance notation
options.thesis: Shape and fill encode meaning exactly.
options.kept: State encoded in line form, not colour alone.

options.label: Grid type specimen
options.thesis: Everything built on a visible grid; one diagonal allowed.
options.case: A typographer's poster, not a household's.
options.kept: One diagonal as the only rebellion: the break is the page's only diagonal.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A smart-home status screen done properly: device rows, status dots, clean type.
canonCard.viewport: Today's page, polished: verdict banner then a list of devices.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other smart-home app by design.
